Luna gets her books and walks toward class.
Hey! Saw your comment about Lost Cause.

_dialogues._content: Fair enough. Lost Cause theories it is.
Okay, then who do you think the masked character really is?
Honestly? I think it's Julian's older brother. Nobody else knew about the cellar key.
Wait, really? I didn't even catch that clue, that actually makes so much sense.
Right?! Look back at chapter twelve, it basically confirms it!
Honestly, I'm mostly just a huge book nerd. Between school and reading, that's pretty much me.
Same. Books, games and music are basically my entire personality.
What kind of music or games are you into, and how's school going?
Mostly indie stuff and cozy story games. School's fine, just way too much homework lately.
Ugh, schoolwork never ends. Glad you still find time to binge good books though.
Nothing special, I go to Rainfall School near Cedar Park. Usually just head straight home afterwards.
Rainfall School? Maybe we live close to each other haha. What streets are you around?
Just a few blocks past Maple Avenue, it's a pretty quiet area.
Oh nice! What time do you usually leave school, and do you always walk home?
Usually around four every day. Yeah, I pretty much take the same route down Maple too.
Gotcha, good to know the area's quiet at least.
You know, you're actually really fun to talk to.
HAHAHA, thanks. You're not that bad either.
We should definitely talk more.
Luna smiles at her phone. For once, she feels like she has found someone who shares her interests.
Heyyy! I saw you joined the Lost Cause community. You seem cool!
Hi! Thanks haha.
GOOOOOD MORNING.
It's wayyyy too early for this HAHAHA.
Someone's grumpy today.
I literally just woke up.
Have fun at school, nerd.
Oh, look. It's our favourite little bookworm.
Did you see what she posted yesterday?
Imagine actually being that embarrassing.
Do you even have friends?

_options.text: Could you just leave me alone?
Ignore them and quietly get your books.
At least I don't spend all day obsessing over other people.

_dialogues._content: Could you just leave me alone? I didn't ask for your opinion.
Whoa, chill. Someone's super sensitive today.
Seriously, we were only joking. Can't you take a joke?
Jokes are supposed to be funny for everyone. Excuse me.
Luna closes her locker firmly, grabs her books and walks into the classroom before they can keep going.
Luna keeps her eyes on her locker, grabs her notebooks without saying a word and pretends they aren't even there.
Hello? Did she suddenly go deaf or is she just scared to talk back?
Ugh, she's boring anyway. Come on, homeroom's starting.
Their muffled laughs follow behind her as Luna slips quietly into the classroom.
At least I don't spend all day obsessing over what other people do.
Excuse me? Wait till everyone online sees you trying to act tough.
Yeah, keep talking like that and see how fast screenshots spread.
Luna's stomach knots as they smirk at each other. She clutches her books tight and enters the classroom.
HEYYYYY.
I noticed you don't post much. You should! Your profile is cute.
Girl, you need to get out there. People need to know you exist.
You should post something. I'll even share it!

_options.text: Post about a favourite book.
Post a selfie without details.
Show uniform and location.

_dialogues._content: Luna takes a photo of her copy of Lost Cause on her desk and posts it without any personal details.
Okay, posted! Nothing crazy, just my favourite book.
Honestly? A little boring haha, people scroll past book covers pretty fast.
Still, you've gotta start somewhere! Keep posting more often, I'll share this one so people notice you.
Alright, thanks Jamie.
Luna snaps a quick selfie against her bedroom wall, making sure nothing personal shows in the background, and hits post.
Uploaded a selfie. Still feels kind of weird though.
Wait, are you kidding?! You look amazing! Why were you even nervous?
Already shared it to my story! Watch the likes roll in.
Haha okay, thanks!
Luna posts a mirror selfie wearing her Rainfall School uniform and tags her location.
Done! Tagged the area too like people usually do.
YES, this is perfect! Sharing it to a couple bigger local pages right now so everyone sees it!
Within minutes, Luna's notifications start buzzing nonstop with views, comments and friend requests from strangers.
Whoa... that got way more attention than I expected.
[A screenshot of Luna's post appears with the caption: Imagine actually thinking this looks good.]
Emma and Sophie have liked and commented on it.
You've got to be kidding me...

_options.text: Save evidence, report it and seek help.
Delete the original and log off.
Comment back and argue.

_dialogues._content: Her hands shake slightly, but Luna screenshots the post, the caption and Emma and Sophie's comments before anything can be deleted.
She submits a harassment report on Connect and saves the screenshots safely so she can show an adult if it escalates.
OMG I saw what happened. Maybe you should post something better next time.
Seriously, Jamie? Right now?
Panicking, Luna hurries to her profile and deletes her original post right away, hoping the whole thing will stop.
She refreshes the feed, only to freeze when she sees the mocking screenshot is still up and people are still laughing in the comments.
Wait... deleting mine didn't take theirs down at all.
OMG I saw what happened. Maybe you should post something better.
Why are you screenshotting my page? Literally get a life.
Emma and Sophie reply within seconds, mocking her in front of everyone. Every back-and-forth pushes the post higher in the feed.
Soon, dozens of unfamiliar accounts are piling into the comments to watch the drama.
OMG I saw what happened. Maybe you should post something better.
Hey, I saw your profile. You seem interesting.
Morning :)
Hey.
How are you?
Pretty tired. School is exhausting.
I get that. You can always talk to me.
Noah is friendly and seems genuinely interested in Luna.
They begin talking about music, hobbies and everyday life.
Luna arrives at school. Emma and Sophie are talking about the picture that was shared online.
Did you see how many people commented?
HAHAHA, she's actually famous now.
Can you stop?
Relax, it's just a joke.
Luna walks away.
You okay? You seemed quiet yesterday.
During lunch, Luna checks her phone and is surprised that Noah remembers.
Can I ask you something?
Sure?
How old are you?

_options.text: I'd rather not share personal information.
Why do you ask?
Tell Noah her age and other personal details.

_dialogues._content: I'd rather not share personal information online, sorry.
Hey, totally fair, I understand.
For a moment Noah keeps things casual, though it doesn't take long before he tries steering back toward personal details.
So are you at least in high school, or do you get stuck with boring afternoon schedules around here too?
Why do you ask?
Just simple curiosity haha, it's nice knowing who I'm talking to.
What do you actually like doing when you're not scrolling on here?
Mostly reading, listening to music and hanging out in my room honestly.
I'm fifteen, going into sophomore year.
Cool, we're basically the same age then.
Noah takes note of her age immediately and keeps pressing further into her private life.
Do your parents check your phone much, or do you usually have the place to yourself after school?
Not really, they're usually busy at work till late.
Do you have a picture of yourself?
Why?
I just want to know who I'm talking to. I'll send one too.

_options.text: Refuse, block and report Noah.
Send a normal selfie.
Send a flirty or revealing selfie.

_dialogues._content: No thanks. I don't send pictures to people I don't know in real life.
Trusting her gut, Luna stops replying right there, blocks Noah and reports his account.
The chat cuts off cleanly—she never sends a photo, and Noah can no longer message her.
Hesitating for a second, Luna sends a normal, casual selfie and waits for Noah to send one back.
Cute :)
Thanks! So are you going to send yours?
Noah leaves her question on read and never sends a photo of his own.
Wanting the attention after a rough few days, Luna chooses a more flirty, dressed-up selfie and hits send.
Wow, you're really pretty.
Seriously, why didn't you say you looked like that? You're gorgeous.
Haha stop, you're too sweet. What about your photo?
After showering her with compliments, Noah's typing indicator vanishes and he suddenly stops replying.
Later that evening, Luna receives a notification.
Look who I found.
Someone has posted her picture on another account without her permission. Luna recognises it immediately.
WHAT??
Did you post this?
Noah does not answer.

_options.text: Save evidence, report, block and tell a trusted adult.
Block Noah and close the app without telling anyone.
Ignore the post and hope it disappears.

_dialogues._content: Okay, breathe... I'm saving proof of all of this right now.
Luna screenshots the reposted photo, the account profile and her entire chat with Noah, then reports and blocks both accounts.
Even though her hands are trembling, she reaches out to someone she trusts so she doesn't have to deal with this alone.
I can't look at this anymore. I just want him gone.
Luna blocks Noah and closes Connect straight away, locking her phone face-down on the bed.
Her screen goes quiet, but she hasn't told anyone what happened—leaving her trapped alone with the anxiety.
Maybe it's just some random repost account. If I ignore it, everyone will forget by tomorrow.
Luna swipes away the alert without saving evidence or reporting the post, trying to pretend it isn't real.
Still, she knows the picture is sitting online where anyone can copy or share it further.
Hey Luna. I think I've seen you around.
Before going to sleep, Luna realises the message request came from an unfamiliar account.
You go to Rainfall School, right?
Luna wakes up feeling uncomfortable after what happened with Noah. When she checks her phone, Connect is full of notifications about the picture.
The unknown account has sent another message. Luna freezes when she realises it knows her school.
Who is this?
Don't worry, I just know some people there.
The account has very little information and no profile picture.
Luna arrives at school. Emma and Sophie are still talking about the picture.
Look who's here.
How's your little internet fame going?
Luna ignores them and goes to class.
Saw you walking home yesterday.
During class, Luna sees the notification and becomes uncomfortable.
You take the same route every day?
Why are you asking?
Just curious. I think I've seen you.

_options.text: Block, report and tell someone about the messages.
Ask how the account knows before deciding what to do.
Share where she walks and when she gets home.

_dialogues._content: Yeah, no. Do not message me again.
Luna ends the conversation immediately, takes screenshots of every message, and blocks and reports the UNKNOWN account.
Shaken, she backs up the screenshots and texts someone she trusts offline to tell them what happened.
Wait... what do you mean you've seen me? How do you know what I look like?
Relax, I've seen you walking near Rainfall School a few times.
Do you always walk by yourself or take the shortcut past the park after last bell?
Luna stares at the screen, unsettled as the stranger keeps fishing for confirmation.
Oh, do you go near Rainfall too? I usually head down Maple Street right after school.
Maple Street? Nice, the quiet way past Cedar Park.
So you're normally getting home around 4:15 then?
Yeah, usually around 4:15 or 4:20 unless I stop by the store.
Without thinking, Luna has confirmed both her usual route home and the exact time she walks it.
Still unsettled by how easily strangers seemed to know where she goes, Luna opens Connect and views her profile as a stranger would.
She scrolls slowly down her own feed—seeing her Rainfall School badge, neighbourhood check-ins, casual posts about walking home and old location tags stacked together.
Wait... I've actually posted all of this?
Seeing every clue laid out in one place hits her hard: anyone could piece together her routine just from her profile.

_options.text: Go private, remove identifying information and review location permissions.
Delete a few posts that reveal personal information.
Leave everything public.

_dialogues._content: Luna switches her profile straight to private, strips her school and neighbourhood from her bio, deletes identifying posts and disables location permissions.
Okay. No stranger gets to read my schedule like a map anymore.
Seeing the privacy lock icon appear next to her name, she finally feels like she is taking control back.
Luna deletes a couple of her most obvious posts and strips one location tag, but leaves her account public and older clues intact.
That's probably enough... nobody scrolls that far back anyway.
Even so, she can't shake the uneasy feeling that too much of her life is still out there.
Luna backs out of Settings without changing anything, leaving her posts, bio and location history wide open.
If I lock everything down now, it feels like letting them win. Everyone posts like this.
Her public profile stays visible to anyone who decides to look closer.
Hey, I saw some of the stuff happening on Connect. Are you okay?
I don't even know anymore.
That sounds rough. Do you want to talk?
Luna hesitates but decides to reply.
I think you should be careful about what people post. Not everything online is what it seems.
Luna decides to talk more with Riley tomorrow.
Good morning! How are you feeling today?
Honestly? Not great.
I understand. I've seen what's been happening, and I wanted to check on you.
Everything has just gotten so complicated.
Sometimes you just need someone to listen.
Riley seems understanding and gives Luna space to explain what has happened.
Luna arrives at school. Emma and Sophie are standing by the lockers.
Well, well, well. Still using that app?
I'd delete it if I were you.
Luna walks past them.
For the first time, she considers telling someone at school what has been happening.
Can I tell you something?
After school, Luna opens Connect.
Sure?
I've been seeing a lot of posts about you. Some people are saying you sent those pictures to everyone.
WHAT? I didn't!
I know. But people are sharing things without checking if they're true.
Riley sends Luna a screenshot of a post discussing the situation.
Apparently Luna sends pictures to random people online.
Luna feels sick reading it.

_options.text: Save evidence, report the misinformation and speak to someone she trusts.
Ignore the post and stop checking the comments.
Publicly confront everyone sharing the post.

_dialogues._content: I'm not arguing with rumours in a comment thread. I'm taking screenshots of the post, who shared it, and reporting all of it.
Luna carefully saves every screenshot, files a misinformation and harassment report, and decides to ask someone she trusts offline for help immediately.
If I stop reading the comments, maybe it'll hurt less.
Luna backs out of the thread and closes the replies—leaving the false rumour unanswered while others keep sharing it.
None of you have any idea what you're talking about—stop spreading lies about me!
Luna argues furiously with everyone in the comments, but every angry reply only pushes the post onto more feeds and draws more mockery.
You know, I think I can help you.
How?
I know someone who can get those posts removed.
Really?
Yeah. But I need you to send me the screenshots and some information about your account.
Luna pauses. Something about the request feels familiar.
She remembers how Alex asked about her school, how Jamie encouraged her to post, how Noah asked for pictures and how the unknown account knew where she went.

_options.text: Refuse to share more information and seek help from a trusted adult.
Ask exactly who will receive the information and why.
Send the screenshots and account details without checking.

_dialogues._content: No, sorry. Asking for my account details feels way too sketchy—I'm not sending anything.
Suit yourself. Was only trying to help.
Riley reads her message and abruptly stops replying. Luna sets her phone down, sure now that she needs help from someone she actually trusts offline.
Wait—who exactly would receive my account details, and why couldn't they report it with just the link?
It's someone my cousin knows who has mod contacts, they just need your login info to verify ownership fast.
Riley tries to brush it off, but the vague explanation only leaves Luna staring at the chat full of doubt.
Okay, sending the screenshots along with my email and account details right now. Just please help me get it down.
Desperate for the nightmare to end, Luna sends everything over without double-checking who is on the other side.
Got them. Leave the rest to us.
The moment the message sends, a cold knot forms in her stomach—she has no idea or control over where her details might end up next.
Luna sits in her bedroom with her phone in her hands and scrolls through the messages from the past five days.
She remembers how excited she was when she first downloaded Connect. At first, it was a place to talk about books and meet people with similar interests.
Now she has experienced bullying, manipulation, unwanted attention and the consequences of sharing personal information.
Her previous decisions have shaped which evidence she saved, which accounts she blocked and whether she has someone she trusts to support her.
Luna opens her messages and decides what to do next.

_options.text: Reach out, preserve evidence, report harmful accounts and secure her privacy.
Take a break and avoid strangers, but keep everything to herself.
Continue using Connect normally and hope it goes away.

_dialogues._content: Luna chooses to reach out to a trusted adult, preserve evidence, report harmful accounts and take control of her online privacy.
Luna takes a break from Connect and avoids interacting with strangers, but keeps everything to herself.
Luna continues using Connect as normal and hopes the situation eventually goes away.
GOOD ENDING
Luna decides to speak to someone she trusts. She shows them the messages, screenshots and posts.
Together, they report the harmful content and take steps to protect her accounts.
The situation does not magically disappear, but Luna understands that she does not have to deal with everything alone.
She opens Connect one final time and reviews her privacy settings.
I guess I have to be more careful about what I share.
Luna closes her laptop.
FADE OUT.
NEUTRAL ENDING
Luna decides to take a break from Connect. She blocks some accounts and deletes a few posts, but never tells anyone what happened.
The situation becomes quieter, but she is still unsure about what information is out there.
She puts her phone away.
Maybe it'll all just go away.
FADE OUT.
BAD ENDING
Luna continues using Connect without addressing what has happened.
More people share the posts, and strangers continue contacting her.
She becomes increasingly isolated and stops talking about what is happening at school and online.
Her phone keeps buzzing.
SFX: BZZZZ. BZZZZ. BZZZZ.
Luna turns it face down.
I wish I had never downloaded this.
FADE OUT.
